title: Red editorial grid (Create. Inspire. / Smart / Wild / Freedom / Bloom / Stillness Horizon)
arc: Manifesto of single words, each one a grid state: a photo cell opens in a hairline grid, the word locks to the cell, then the grid collapses to the next word (ladder of single nouns, one shared grid, ends by collapsing to a point).
world: White paper ground, hairline crimson grid lines that are the only furniture, one condensed heavy red grotesque for the hero word, tiny red caption blocks in the grid corners, full-colour photo only ever inside a grid cell (the second photo goes desaturated full-bleed first).
actor: The grid itself: its crossing lines are the camera and the layout engine. Cells slide, split and swallow each other; a cell is a photo window, a red fill, or empty paper. The word is pinned to a cell edge and travels with it.

lines.show: Two small red words sit either side of a vertical grid line at the exact crossing of two hairlines; the lines slide in from the page edges to cross before the words appear, so the words look hung on the lines rather than placed.
lines.handoff: The vertical line stays; the cell between the words becomes the slot where the next word will drop.

lines.line: THIS IS WHERE IT BEGINS  /  A STORY IN MOTION
lines.show: Two micro-captions (three short stacked lines each) sit in the lower cells diagonally opposite each other, bottom-left under the left word and bottom-right under the right word; they ride the grid as it drifts, never animating on their own.
lines.handoff: Captions stay in their cells; only the hero cell changes, so the page reads as one sheet re-cut.

lines.show: The hero word pops in a notch below the centre crossing, between the two lines, scaling from the crossing outward; ~1.3 s later the cell behind it floods solid red and the word flips to white (a flash-fill), then the fill drops away again.
lines.handoff: The red fill is the 'impact'; when it drains, the grid slides sideways and the next word's photo cell slides in from the right.

lines.show: A bird photo cell slides in left of the word as the grid pans, cropped exactly to a grid rectangle; WILD sits at the cell's top-right corner, partly clipped by the frame edge on arrival and settling in. Captions swap to SMALL THINGS CARRY BIG SONGS (left) / FREE IS A FEELING and EVERY VOICE DESERVES TO BE HEARD (right).
lines.handoff: The photo cell shrinks toward the left edge while the word stays, leaving a thin dark sliver that becomes the next word's anchor.

lines.show: The bird photo breathes slowly (slight push-in, the animal sings) while the grid sits still: the only movement in the frame is the subject, which is the point of the hold.
lines.handoff: Cell shrinks to a small dark chip at lower left.

lines.show: The photo cell collapses to a small dark chip and a big white cell opens to its right; the long word FREEDOM is set across that wide cell, so word width = cell width.
lines.handoff: The chip is replaced by the next photo growing from the same lower-left corner.

lines.show: A desaturated blossom photo fills the whole frame in grey; the grid appears on top; a small colour cutout of the blossom opens in a lower-left cell (the only colour), BLOOM sits at its top-right edge. The cutout later grows and shifts up-right so colour 'blooms' across cells while the grey remains.
lines.handoff: Colour cell shrinks and the page flashes back to white paper for the lake photo.

lines.show: A wide lake landscape fills one cell with a small red boat; a brief hold, then the cell shrinks as the grid re-divides around it.
lines.handoff: The cell shrinks to a small centre rectangle that becomes the hinge between two words.

lines.show: STILLNESS slides in at the left of the shrunken photo cell and HORIZON drops to its lower right, diagonal around the photo like the lines cross at the cell corners; captions SOME JOURNEYS MOVE SLOW and STILLNESS HAS ITS OWN SOUND fill the small cells.
lines.handoff: The photo cell shrinks to a point and the two words close up to touch at that point.

lines.show: The photo shrinks to nothing; the two heavy words meet at the crossing point, STILLNESS left-above, HORIZON right-below, grid lines becoming a single cross through the lockup. Everything stops.

techniques: hairline grid as layout and camera
word pinned to a cell edge
flash-fill (cell floods solid colour then drains)
cell shrinks to a point as the exit
desaturated full-bleed with a colour window
captions stay put while the hero cell changes
lessons: Make one structural device (the grid) do all the staging: cells open for photos, flood for impact, collapse for exits; no extra transitions needed.
Pin the hero word to a corner of the moving cell so the word and the picture feel like one object; set long words across a wide cell.
Keep chrome static (captions, hairlines) and let one thing change at a time; the stillness around it is what makes the change read.
Hold a living photo (the singing bird, the boat) in a quiet frame; motion in the subject is the beat between grid moves.
Reserve colour: red for type and lines, full colour only inside a cell, desaturate the rest so each photo reads as a reveal.
End by collapsing the picture to a point and letting the words touch, the grid's last move is its resolve.
